au-yarra-valley.climate: Cool conditions, with altitude and exposure creating substantial differences between vineyards.

wines.name: Yarra Valley Pinot Noir
wines.description: Pinot Noir is one of the Yarra Valley's signature wines. Red fruit and floral aromas sit above a supple palate; cooler sites often emphasise freshness, while oak and whole-bunch fermentation can add spice and savoury detail.

tastingProfile.style: Fragrant, fresh Pinot Noir with supple red fruit and fine tannins

wines.agingPotential: Enjoy young; structured examples develop with cellaring

wines.name: Yarra Valley Chardonnay
wines.description: Yarra Valley Chardonnay commonly balances citrus and stone fruit with lively acidity. Barrel fermentation and lees ageing can add texture and toasted-nut character, although the amount of oak varies considerably between producers.

tastingProfile.style: Citrus-led Chardonnay with fresh acidity and a gently textured palate

wines.agingPotential: Enjoy young; concentrated examples can develop in bottle

wines.name: Yarra Valley Cabernet Sauvignon
wines.description: Cabernet Sauvignon has a long history in the Yarra Valley. Its cooler-climate expression often combines blackcurrant fruit with leafy freshness and a firm structure; some producers blend it with other Bordeaux varieties.

tastingProfile.style: Structured Cabernet with dark fruit, leafy freshness and fine-grained tannins

wines.agingPotential: Structured examples are suited to cellaring

sources.label: Yering Station: Yarra Valley Cabernet Sauvignon

wines.name: Yarra Valley Shiraz / Syrah
wines.description: Yarra Valley Shiraz is also labelled Syrah, particularly where producers emphasise a savoury, cool-climate style. Berry fruit, floral lift and peppery spice often accompany a medium-weight palate.

tastingProfile.style: Peppery, medium-bodied Syrah with fresh berry fruit and savoury detail

wines.agingPotential: Enjoy young or cellar structured examples

au-clare-valley.climate: Warm days and cooler nights; elevation and varied exposures help retain freshness.

wines.name: Clare Valley Riesling
wines.description: Dry Riesling is Clare Valley's best-known white wine. Lime and lemon flavours meet a taut, refreshing palate, usually without obvious oak. Mature examples can gain honeyed and toasty complexity while retaining their acid backbone.

tastingProfile.style: Dry, lime-driven Riesling with a light body and incisive acidity

wines.agingPotential: Enjoy fresh; fine examples can age for many years

sources.label: Wine Australia: Clare Valley Estate Riesling

wines.name: Clare Valley Shiraz
wines.description: Clare Valley also produces substantial red wines. Its Shiraz typically has ripe dark fruit and spice, with enough structure and freshness to balance the richness. Oak maturation can add savoury and toasted notes.

tastingProfile.style: Rich, dark-fruited Shiraz with rounded texture and balancing structure

wines.agingPotential: Enjoy young; concentrated examples can develop with age

wines.name: Clare Valley Cabernet Sauvignon
wines.description: Cabernet Sauvignon is an established Clare Valley red. Blackcurrant fruit, herbal detail and firm tannins give the wines their shape; ripeness and oak treatment vary with vineyard and producer.

tastingProfile.style: Firm, dark-fruited Cabernet with herbal freshness and a structured finish

wines.agingPotential: Structured examples benefit from bottle age

sources.label: Taylors: St Andrews Clare Valley Cabernet Sauvignon

au-margaret-river.climate: Maritime conditions moderated by the Indian and Southern Oceans.

wines.name: Margaret River Cabernet Sauvignon
wines.description: Margaret River Cabernet combines aromatic dark fruit with fine tannins. It may include small amounts of other Bordeaux varieties; the most structured examples develop well in bottle.

tastingProfile.style: Perfumed Cabernet with fine tannins and fresh, concentrated fruit

wines.agingPotential: Fine examples are suited to long-term cellaring

wines.name: Margaret River Chardonnay
wines.description: Concentrated fruit and a fresh acid line underpin Margaret River Chardonnay. Barrel fermentation and lees ageing often contribute texture without obscuring its citrus and stone-fruit character.

tastingProfile.style: Layered Chardonnay with concentrated fruit, texture and lively acidity

wines.agingPotential: Enjoy young or cellar concentrated examples

wines.name: Margaret River Semillon–Sauvignon Blanc
wines.description: This regional white blend brings together Sauvignon Blanc's aromatic lift and Semillon's texture. Fresh, stainless-steel-fermented examples are common, alongside more textured barrel-influenced versions.

tastingProfile.style: Crisp, aromatic white blend with bright fruit and gentle texture

wines.agingPotential: Fresh styles are best enjoyed young

wines.name: Margaret River Shiraz
wines.description: Margaret River Shiraz often emphasises fragrance and medium-bodied balance. Its berry fruit and spice suit a savoury style, sometimes labelled Syrah.

tastingProfile.style: Fragrant, medium-bodied Shiraz with berry fruit and savoury spice

wines.agingPotential: Enjoy young or cellar structured examples

au-coonawarra.climate: Cool maritime conditions influenced by the Southern Ocean.

wines.name: Coonawarra Shiraz
wines.description: Coonawarra has a long Shiraz tradition alongside its celebrated Cabernet Sauvignon. Berry and plum fruit, pepper and floral notes often meet a savoury palate with more restraint than many warmer-climate Australian examples.

tastingProfile.style: Savoury Shiraz with berry fruit, pepper and a fresh, structured palate

wines.agingPotential: Enjoy young; structured wines can develop in bottle
